analyses.current_state: On Epoch AI's FrontierMath v2 (Tiers 1-3) benchmark leaderboard evaluated via Python-enabled iterative reasoning on private math problems, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol leads with a score of 89.00%. On Epoch AI's FrontierMath v2 (Tier 4) leaderboard evaluating research-level mathematics expansion problems, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol achieves a leading score of 83.00%.
analyses.reference_class: Iterative Python-enabled reasoning models evaluated on Epoch AI FrontierMath v2 math problem tiers
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is driven by advanced Python-enabled iterative reasoning loops and fine-tuning on research-level mathematics; downward pressure stems from the strictness of FrontierMath v2 problem validation (following correction of errors in 42% of problems) and the intrinsic difficulty of Tier 4 expansion problems.
scenarios: Sol maintains its lead on FrontierMath v2 as further test-time compute optimizations are deployed.
Rival models surpass Sol's 89.00% Tiers 1-3 and 83.00% Tier 4 scores via newly released model architectures.
analyses.key_uncertainty: Exact internal weights, training compute budgets, and fine-tuning details for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard for ARC-AGI-1 semi-private set evaluation, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna achieves 90.7% accuracy at a cost of $0.07 per task under max reasoning effort. On the official ARC Prize leaderboard for ARC-AGI-2 semi-private set evaluation, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna scores 59.6% accuracy at $0.18 per task under max reasoning effort.
analyses.reference_class: Reasoning models evaluated on official ARC Prize semi-private sets (ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2)
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is generated by max reasoning effort execution and test-time compute scaling; downward pressure on ARC-AGI-2 relative to ARC-AGI-1 is driven by the substantially higher complexity and out-of-distribution reasoning required by the ARC-AGI-2 task set.
scenarios: Luna's task execution cost per task shifts down as hardware efficiency improves, allowing higher inference scaling.
Future benchmark iterations expose limitations in Luna's generalization capability on ARC-AGI-2.
analyses.key_uncertainty: Exact token usage breakdown and internal compute overhead per task beyond the reported dollar costs.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scores 97.5% on ARC-AGI-1, 90.4% on ARC-AGI-2, and 30.16% on ARC-AGI-3.
analyses.reference_class: Frontier multimodal and reasoning models evaluated across ARC-AGI benchmark tiers (1, 2, and 3)
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is driven by advanced architectural updates and broad generalization capabilities on ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2; downward pressure is caused by the extreme out-of-distribution novelty of ARC-AGI-3, where performance drops sharply to 30.16%.
scenarios: Subsequent Anthropic releases dramatically improve ARC-AGI-3 performance by targeting novel abstraction tasks.
Performance plateaus on ARC-AGI-3 due to foundational limitations in zero-shot visual abstraction.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The specific reasoning settings and inference cost per task associated with Claude Opus 5 on the ARC Prize leaderboard.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash achieves 91.2% on ARC-AGI-1 and 60.4% on ARC-AGI-2.
analyses.reference_class: Speed-optimized frontier model variants evaluated on ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 semi-private sets
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure comes from efficient model design and broad context utilization; downward pressure stems from optimization trade-offs prioritizing execution speed over deep iterative test-time reasoning.
scenarios: Gemini 3.6 Flash variants scale up test-time reasoning to close the gap on ARC-AGI-2.
The model maintains its speed-cost profile while competitors pull further ahead on complex abstraction tasks.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The compute budget and hardware infrastructure utilized by Google to run Gemini 3.6 Flash on the ARC Prize leaderboard.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, xAI's Grok 4.5 achieves an 87.2% score on ARC-AGI-1, 52.6% on ARC-AGI-2, and 0.32% on ARC-AGI-3.
analyses.reference_class: Frontier models evaluated across progressive ARC-AGI complexity tiers (1 through 3)
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is supported by model scaling and pre-training data curation; downward pressure is reflected in the near-zero performance (0.32%) on ARC-AGI-3, illustrating the difficulty unadapted base models face on extreme abstraction tiers.
scenarios: xAI deploys specialized reasoning search algorithms to lift Grok 4.5's ARC-AGI-3 score above single digits.
Grok 4.5 remains constrained on Tier 3 abstraction tasks while focusing product mix on enterprise conversational utilities.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The training dataset composition and reasoning framework integration implemented in Grok 4.5.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 scores 94.5% on ARC-AGI-1 and 60.4% on ARC-AGI-2.
analyses.reference_class: International frontier models evaluated on standardized ARC-AGI benchmark sets
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is driven by effective context handling and architectural refinement; downward pressure is exerted by the inherent difficulty step-up between ARC-AGI-1 (94.5%) and ARC-AGI-2 (60.4%).
scenarios: Kimi K3 introduces test-time search modules that elevate its ARC-AGI-2 score into the 80% range.
Performance stabilizes as the product mix emphasizes long-context document processing over grid-based abstraction.
analyses.key_uncertainty: Inference pricing structures and latency profiles associated with Kimi K3 evaluations.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, DeepSeek's DeepSeek V4 Flash scores 89.0% on ARC-AGI-1 and 61.4% on ARC-AGI-2.
analyses.reference_class: Cost-optimized flash model architectures evaluated on ARC-AGI semi-private leaderboards
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is driven by efficient mixture-of-experts routing and low-latency inference design; downward pressure results from resource constraints limiting exhaustive search-based problem solving.
scenarios: DeepSeek releases a heavier reasoning variant that surpasses current V4 Flash scores on ARC-AGI-2.
V4 Flash serves as a cost-efficient baseline while competitors absorb higher compute costs for marginal accuracy gains.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The hardware cluster specifications and training cost efficiency metrics behind DeepSeek V4 Flash.

analyses.current_state: On the official ARC Prize leaderboard, Thinking Machines' Inkling Small (xHigh reasoning setting) achieves 84.0% on ARC-AGI-1 and 40.1% on ARC-AGI-2 at $0.233 per task.
analyses.reference_class: Compact reasoning models evaluated at high test-time compute settings on ARC-AGI leaderboards
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure is enabled by the xHigh reasoning setting, which increases compute per task to boost accuracy; downward pressure is created by high execution costs ($0.233 per task) relative to larger models.
scenarios: Inkling Small achieves higher parameter efficiency, reducing the cost per task while maintaining the xHigh reasoning accuracy.
Higher unit costs constrain widespread adoption of the xHigh setting in production environments.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The architectural scale of Inkling Small and the specific mechanics of its xHigh reasoning loop.

analyses.current_state: Epoch AI released FrontierMath v2 on June 12, 2026, correcting errors in 42% of problems across a dataset consisting of 338 total problems (295 in Tiers 1-3 base set and 43 in Tier 4 expansion set).
analyses.reference_class: Expert-vetted mathematical benchmark datasets designed for frontier AI evaluation
analyses.mechanisms: Upward pressure on benchmark reliability comes from rigorous error correction (fixing 42% of problems); downward pressure on baseline scores stems from the inclusion of highly complex Tier 4 expansion problems.
scenarios: Subsequent benchmark revisions introduce further problem tiers to prevent score saturation.
Model performance on FrontierMath v2 approaches high accuracy, prompting the creation of a v3 dataset.
analyses.key_uncertainty: The complete breakdown and exact formulation of all 338 individual problems within the updated FrontierMath v2 private release.

scenarios: Claude Fable 5 sets the benchmark standard for forthcoming evaluation rounds until new reasoning paradigms emerge.
Rival labs deploy higher inference budgets to surpass Fable 5's 98.5% ARC-AGI-1 score.
